junction.name: South Conduit Avenue & Hook Creek Boulevard, New York City

claims.text: South Conduit Avenue & Hook Creek Boulevard had 64 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 15 pedestrians injured, 7 cyclists injured and 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $4.4 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the city's own past installs passed the causal gate), worth $134,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 1.9 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $657,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for S CONDUIT AVE (NY 27), South Conduit Avenue, Hook Creek Boulevard (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 31, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 13.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
